turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
I, uh... I came in because I just keep feeling like I’ve completely let my family down by taking on this mortgage. It’s... it's just a lot. The house actually has this huge oak tree in the front yard, which is nice, but the roots are totally messing up the concrete on the driveway. I spent like three hours watching YouTube videos on how to fix driveway cracks last weekend, but then the algorithm just started showing me videos of guys building log cabins from scratch out in the woods, and I ended up watching those until like 3 AM. I always thought it'd be cool to just live off the grid like that, you know? Not have to worry about property taxes or HOA fees... 

But, um, what was I saying? Right, the mortgage. It just weighs on me so much. Like, every small mistake I make at work—I wait tables, so if I drop a fork or punch in the wrong appetizer—it just proves I’m completely useless. I just get this heavy feeling that I deserve whatever bad things happen to me.

turns.doctor_question: Have you lost interest or pleasure in doing things you normally enjoy?
turns.patient_response:
Lost interest? Um, yeah, I'd say so. Like, I used to always joke around with the regulars at the restaurant, and I'd usually text my brother right after my shifts to catch up. 

My brother actually just got one of those new folding smartphones. It's so weird, it looks like a little square coaster from the outside but then it opens up into this giant screen. I don't really get why you'd want a screen with a visible crease right down the middle of it, honestly. Plus, he dropped it like two days after he bought it, which is just classic him. He's always been super clumsy. When we were kids, he knocked over our mom's favorite lamp—it was this really ugly ceramic owl, but she loved it for some reason—and he tried to glue it back together with just regular white school glue. It looked absolutely terrible, you could see the glue dripping down the owl's beak. 

But, uh... sorry, what were you asking? Oh, right, enjoying things. Yeah, I just don't really do any of that anymore. I mostly just keep my face straight at work now, say only what I have to, and get it over with. And when my brother texts me, I just let the messages sit there. I just don't really feel the pull to answer anybody.

turns.doctor_question: During this time, have you had any thoughts of death or thoughts of wanting to hurt yourself?
turns.patient_response:
Thoughts of death? Um... I mean, I don't have a plan to hurt myself or anything like that. But sometimes, when I'm lying awake before an early shift... 

I hate those early shifts, honestly. You have to be there at like 5:30 in the morning to set up the coffee stations and roll the silverware. And the silverware is always still hot from the dishwasher, which sounds nice, but it actually kind of burns your fingers if you're not careful. One time, the dishwasher—this guy named Leo, who is super into amateur wrestling—he accidentally loaded a plastic ramekin into the high-heat cycle and it completely melted over the heating element. The whole kitchen smelled like burning tires for three days. We had to keep all the back doors propped open, which let all these flies in, and the manager was furious. He made Leo buy these special fly traps that look like little paper lanterns, but they didn't even work. 

But, um, anyway... yeah. When I'm lying awake before those shifts, I just... I sometimes think it would be easier if I just didn't wake up. Like, if I just didn't have to get out of bed and keep failing at everything, you know? It just feels like it would be a relief.

symptom_reasoning.S030: The patient expresses feelings of worthlessness by stating they feel like they 'keep failing at everything.'
symptom_reasoning.S032: The patient confirms passive thoughts of death, stating they sometimes think it would be easier if they just didn't wake up, even though they deny having a specific plan for self-harm.
